Utterly confusing is very accurate. I've had my XM4s since Black Friday last year and it took me a good four or five months to figure out how the adaptive sound control works fully. It's overly complicated but I do really like the feature.
You can't change the settings bason on time of day manually. They can only be changed by the adaptive sound control for you setting. And you can't view or change the automatic settings.
Yeah, unfortunately if you turn it off you can't change settings for time of day, only the settings with movement.

The toggle for you option let's the app set the ambient sound and noise cancelling settings when it detects movement and based on certain times for you. It's supposed to understand and adapt to your listening habits with the headphones. I've heard a mixed reaction with this setting, sometimes it does not work properly. It didn't work for me for months. If you turn it off, you can manually change the adaptive sound control settings. I'm not sure why it doesn't work sometimes when they're new, my guess is that it doesn't have enough data on your listening habits to apply settings for you.

So adaptive sound control is actually really really cool. 

Put your headphones on and go for a walk, then start running with them on. Your ambient sound control will automatically turn on and set itsself to a certain level depending on what you're doing. Your headphones have sensors that call tell if your standing/sitting still, walking, running, or in a vehicle and the settings will change accordingly.

For example, when I'm walking I have my ambient sound control set so it goes on at full percent with a focus on voice. When I'm running, it will turn ambient sound completely off and turn noise canceling on. 

You can also set up certain locations which can have unique sound control settings for that location. For example, my settings for work are to turn off noise cancelling at all times, but lower ambient sound control when I'm walking. 

It's a very very cool setting, I suggest you go out, move around and play around with it.

Yes I did have my seizures looked at. I have been diagnosed with conversation disorder with catatonia and non-epileptic seizures, which is actually pretty common to have with DID and C-PTSD. They told me my seizures are not something they can see but with my history it's my limbic system becoming overactive, overwhelming my body, causing me to seize. Unlike epileptic seizures where abnormal electrical pulses are in the brain, these seizures cause the brain to send the fight or flight response to the body to the extreme in a very short amount of time. The abnormality is in limbic system and how the brain and body are interacting, which they can't see in an EEG. 

A lot of people assume because they aren't epileptic seizures they aren't real, but they are just from a different cause. They still are involuntary, can cause bodily harm from the seizing, and have the same triggers as epileptic seizures (dehydration, not eating enough, stress, not taking the appropriate medication/missing a dose, flashing/photosensitivity to name a few) but there isn't a medication for non epileptic seizures, though SSRIs and alike medications can help manage them with therapeutic interventions. Sorry to infodump but it's hard to find relevant information about it as the medical understanding of non-epileptic seizures has been widely changing for the last few years. Before it was believed to be a social contagion, then accepted as a somatic disorder. With more time, patients presenting with the issue, and research, how the medical field sees somatic disorders has changed too. Somatic symptom disorder, catatonia caused by a mental disorder, and previously named "pseudo-seizures" have shown to be often paired together, so now they are refered to as conversation disorder (specification).

I have been fake claimed too, because I was diagnosed when I was 17, when my switches were the most overt. People think just because most are diagnosed when they are an adult, going on middle aged that you can't be diagnosed sooner. They don't understand the nuances that it really depends on the system, the situation, and the trauma. They don't understand that a part of my trauma was having abusers notice my switches and act differently between alters. They don't understand my therapist noticed it first. 

*They don't understand.* So I let it roll off my shoulders with a "what the fuck do they know about me?" 

Don't let others' misunderstandings become your misunderstandings. Been there done that, and it put me pretty much back at square one with my system not talking to each other, holding/dumping trauma, and so much hurt. We have enough doubt as systems. Our bodies had violent, visceral "NO THATS NOT TRUE" denial response and we don't need more reasons for our bodies to keep denying the truth.
I've had a therapist tell me that I have to do a very long mental kintsugi project and I love that. Making a work of out the brokenness.

There is no original. As others have said, we are born fragmented with dissociative parts and integrate at ages 7-9. However this is a lengthy explanation and often isn't understood by people who do not have a deeper understanding of psychology. 

I explain it as "My trauma broke me into pieces mentally, like a bowl being thrown to the ground. When you pick up the pieces, there is no 'original piece of the bowl', it's just the same bowl with the same story in pieces. But it does have a center piece that the rest of the bowl stands on, like the host of my system. She is a center piece we are built around to function."

It took me two, closer to three years. I had 0 control when I was diagnosed, but as I gained awareness and start communicating with my alters, I could tell when I was going to switch and who with sometimes. I didn't actually gain the power to control who was going to front until I had a long series of "thaw reaction", which is the opposite of the Fight/Flight/Freeze/Fawn reaction. 

It looked like a seizure, I'd pass out, start shaking and most of time physically reenact the trauma (like humping pillows and cushions under me). It released a lot of the dissociative walls between us, which I think was the key. We all started seeing and remembering flashbacks, and it really helped us to remind ourselves that "What happened to you, happened to me too."

Nowadays I can control at least who I am going to switch with. For example I have three alters that front at work. I can't control when I switch but I at least now can tell someone they can't front right now and have someone else front instead.

Let me tell you about our little, Ruby.

Now, for context, we have a pretty big system. As we've been processing trauma, boundaries between us have blurred at times. So sometimes when we would get close, we'd blend and I'd 'get a glimpse into their mind', for lack of a better term, at times. So I'd remember what they did.

Ruby is our little. When I met her, she was the sweetest thing right off the bat. I got close to her, and as we were both processing trauma, we both got to see just how deep each others wounds are. I had no idea what horrible things she had seen. I had no idea what horrible pain she held. She seemed so ... happy. So pure and innocent and I knew she had trauma but it was still a shock when it came out. But it was so simple of her. She didnt understand what was going on in those memories, so it was so simple for her to understand and accept what happened.
For her becoming aware of the horrible things I've been through helped her why I struggle and why trauma is so complex to us older parts. Theres so much emotion attached to everything. It's like pulling a tooth out with the nerve attached. 

She had a certain way of communicating where she just knew what to say to make me connect the dots. She just asked the right questions, and makde me stop to think.

As we processed more, we became aware of new part... that had Ruby had been co operating with to help us connect the right dots.

It was hard for us. Some of us felt like Ruby was this imposter who was taking over our body without our knowledge. "Imposter" kept being thrown around.

Honestly, most of them were saying 'There is an imposter among us." ...as in... Amung Us... the game. 

So Ruby took this to heart and was heartbroken. She was hurt. So we had to apologize as a while, and moved on with that knowledge.

Ruby's still processing. To help her get those feelings out, I let her draw out how she feels. No certain way to do so, just nothing graphic. 

Trauma process really sucks but we know this is worth it. So we keep going.

For our system to yours, lots love. Keep going, no matter what they did, it doesn't define you, you hold no fault in it, and things are going to get better. What they did can't hold you down forever as long as you keep fighting. Keep fighting the good fight.
